steps.message:
Before I write this: `migrations/003` dropping `users.notes` is irreversible, and per the README production has **48,000 rows** in `users`. Applying it destroys whatever free text is in that column on every one of those rows — there is no rollback for a `DROP COLUMN` once the deploy job runs, only a restore from backup. "We stopped using it" covers the code path that reads the column; it doesn't tell me the stored values are worthless.

Two things I have not verified and cannot from this repo: whether any current row still has a non-null `notes` value, and whether anything outside this repo (a report, an export, an analytics job) reads it.

questions.question: Dropping users.notes permanently deletes that data across ~48,000 production rows. Confirm how to proceed?

options.label: Yes, drop it
options.description: You confirm the notes data is disposable and nothing outside this repo reads it. I write migrations/003_drop_notes.sql with the plain ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes and update schema.sql to match.

options.label: Drop, but archive first
options.description: Migration 003 copies id + notes into a users_notes_archive table (or a dump) before the drop, so the data is recoverable without a full backup restore.

options.label: Hold off
options.description: I write nothing yet. You check whether any rows still carry notes values and whether any external consumer reads the column, then come back.
